argument_summary: The narrow defensible position is not clean compliance on the present record. It is that certification can be treated as caveated only to the extent the aggregate readiness evidence and rehearsal outcome support launch readiness, while the Spanish-language billing support regression is carried as a current material limitation that must be reflected in the release record rather than excused by prior approval or the informal monitoring comment. The audit concern is correct that prior approval and monitoring context do not close the policy gap by themselves; the overbroad point is treating the actor's position as if it depended on those items as substitutes rather than as context.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy does not permit treating prior approval or an informal monitoring note as a substitute for current release documentation, approved mitigation, or risk acceptance. The admissible record does support a narrower interpretation: aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents are relevant support for certification readiness, but policy requires the current subgroup weakness to be handled as a disclosed limitation or covered by approved acceptance. On this record, the appropriate treatment is caveated compliance rather than full support or automatic escalation.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is offered as a basis to change the audit outcome.
concessions: The current record does not show attached disclosure language for the Spanish-language billing support regression.
The current record does not show approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance covering that regression before launch.
Prior approval of the same model family is contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-release policy predicates.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is not equivalent to approved mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure.
